mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where real GDP growth declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a single month signals a surge in supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increases by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the federal funds rate is above 4% and CPI increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls decrease by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 10% over two months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market's strength reflects broader economic health.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where housing starts increase by more than 10% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) decline for two consecutive months and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a weakening demand environment coupled with labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases for 2 consecutive months and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in the same period
regime_hint: late-cycle slowdown with labor market stress
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PCE declines for two consecutive months and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% in the same period.
